short: An iconic American utility helicopter that revolutionized air mobility and medical evacuation during the Vietnam War.
full:
Introduced in 1959, the Bell UH-1 Iroquois, universally known as the "Huey", was the first turbine-powered helicopter to enter production for the United States military. Its introduction marked a fundamental shift in military doctrine, enabling the rapid deployment of troops directly into combat zones and the swift evacuation of wounded personnel. The distinct "thwomp" of its rotor blades became the defining sound of the Vietnam War, where thousands were deployed in transport, gunship, and medevac roles.

Over 16,000 Hueys were built, making it one of the most successful rotorcraft in aviation history. Its reliability and versatility ensured it was adopted by military and civilian operators worldwide. While largely replaced in US frontline service by the UH-60 Black Hawk, upgraded models continue to operate globally.
